SMTO-CMP-0034 — The AI added a summary you didn't ask for

GUID: 140c9e68-d9fa-4088-8637-844047c818b7
Slug: completion-unrequested-recap
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • This task was set to finish without a written summary, but the AI's finish included one. SMTO asked the AI to finish without it. The work itself isn't affected.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the task still shows Running, wait. SMTO has asked the AI to finish without the extra summary, and it normally does this by itself. Only the way the AI finished is wrong, so nothing has to be redone.
  2. If the task stops as Partial · resumable, expand the task and confirm the steps you wanted are marked Completed. This shows whether the work is done even though the finish wasn't accepted.
  3. If you do want a summary, send a message asking SMTO to summarize what it did. SMTO accepts a summary when you ask for one.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed, either without a summary or with the summary you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rerun the task to get rid of the summary; that would repeat its steps.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Completion was rejected because summarize_result is off and the terminal output contract is none, yet the declaration supplied an unrequested recap message (historical diagnostic for legacy runs).

What this means

  • With summarization disabled and no requested output, completion supplies an unsolicited message instead of the accepted action-only result. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • With summarization disabled and no requested output, completion supplies an unsolicited message instead of the accepted action-only result.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare effective summarize_result and accepted output requirements while preserving requested deliverables.

How to fix it

  • Compare the run's effective summarize_result and terminal_output_contract with the declared message; the model should resubmit completion with no message while preserving any explicitly requested output. Current code no longer raises unrequested_recap directly and only maps it to the completion.output_contract Agent Check (Enforce requested output contract), so confirm whether the run predates the version-1 reply policy.
  • Preserve the requested final result; do not replace it with an unrequested recap.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Completion respects the intended no-recap contract without discarding required output.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors
